name: Sodium cyanide
typicalUses: SN2 with primary/secondary halides: nitriles (adds one carbon)
chemoselectivity: Ambident: alkylation usually on carbon (nitrile); silver cyanide favours the isocyanide
pitfalls: Acid releases HCN gas, which is extremely toxic

name: Sodium azide
typicalUses: SN2 to alkyl azides, then reduction to primary amines
chemoselectivity: An excellent nucleophile but a weak base, so substitution beats elimination
pitfalls: HN₃ is toxic and explosive; heavy-metal azides are explosive; never use CH₂Cl₂ as solvent (diazidomethane)

name: Triphenylphosphine
typicalUses: Staudinger reduction of azides to amines (with water)
Appel (alcohol → alkyl halide) and Mitsunobu reactions
chemoselectivity: Nucleophilic at P; ends up as Ph₃P=O, whose strong P=O bond drives these reactions
pitfalls: Removing the Ph₃P=O by-product is a classic purification headache

name: Sodium iodide in acetone
typicalUses: Finkelstein reaction: R–Cl or R–Br → R–I
chemoselectivity: Driven by precipitation of NaCl/NaBr, which are insoluble in acetone
pitfalls: I⁻ is both an excellent nucleophile and an excellent leaving group
